# smyx-autism-stereotyped-behavior-detect-analysis 1.0.3 Changelog

- Internal updates to `dao.py` and `util.py` scripts in `skills/smyx_common/scripts/`.
- Removed legacy documentation file `skill-card.md`.
- No changes to end-user workflow or main feature set.

**Major update: The skill now handles user identity automatically, removing the need for user-provided IDs. Documentation and usage instructions updated accordingly.**

- Internalizes all user identity handling—users are no longer asked to provide usernames, phone numbers, or open-id; all such parameters are managed within the system.
- Updated documentation and example commands: removed references to any user identity fields in both user-facing prompts and technical instructions.
- Clarified and tightened privacy protections: explicit prohibition on asking for or exposing user identity values at any stage.
- Adjusted workflow and notes to reflect a more streamlined, user-friendly process.
- Modernized SKILL.md structure and presentation, with clearer resource indexing and scenario tables.
- Removed obsolete files and cleaned up scripts to reflect the new authentication/identity model.

- Updated config file path logic and documentation for open-id lookup, clarifying directory structure and priority.
- Clarified project license as MIT-0.
- Streamlined and shortened the skill description for better readability.
- Removed redundant or deprecated documentation files (skill-card.md).
- Updated internal references to configuration and requirement files in line with path and structure changes.

Initial release of smyx-autism-stereotyped-behavior-detect-analysis

- Provides automated detection of key stereotyped behaviors in children (e.g., spinning, hand flapping, body rocking) from fixed-camera videos using pose estimation and temporal action detection.
- Generates frequency and duration statistics of each behavior, with daily and weekly reports to support rehabilitation planning.
- Enables real-time, objective monitoring for therapists and parents to track intervention effects and personalize therapy.
- Strict privacy and process controls: requires open-id verification before use, prohibits local memory report retrieval, and enforces cloud-based report querying.
- Designed for integration into rehabilitation center systems or home apps; supports structured, trend-based behavior summaries.
